subject: Orbitly launch: traffic runway, rate guardrails & product clarifications
messages:
From: Sara Chen <sara@orbitly.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim O'Neill <tim@orbitly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Orbitly Nov 18-20 launch window — temporary rate uplift request & product Qs

Diego,

Quick context: Orbitly is planning a staged public rollout on Nov 18 with a peak marketing-driven spike expected Nov 19. We ran an internal sim and attached a traffic matrix that shows expected ingress across regions. Short version: we need a temporary rate uplift and guidance on warmup best practices.

What we think we need (prelim):
- Peak concurrent requests: ~950 RPS during a 45-minute peak on Nov 19
- Sustained token throughput during peak: ~320k tokens/min (chat-style requests, ~230 tokens/response avg)
- Expected 70% chat/interactive, 30% async batch
- Live traffic profile attached (orbitly_traffic_matrix.csv)

Two product questions:
1) Does Redwood support pre-warming KV/prefix caches or do we need to prime traffic?
2) If we request a temporary dedicated pool, what model variants do you recommend for balancing latency vs cost?

Can you confirm feasibility and what you need from us to lock a temporary uplift? We'd like confirmation by EOD Wednesday Nov 4 to finalize launch comms.

Thanks — appreciate the quick review.

Sara Chen
Product Manager, Orbitly
(sara@orbitly.ai)
(attachment: orbitly_traffic_matrix.csv)

I'll draft a neat mutual action plan once we have numbers. Attach: orbitly_traffic_matrix.csv (forwarded).

Diego / all — dug into the traffic matrix and ran a quick perf estimate. Short answers first: feasible with a temporary dedicated pool and a staged canary. Details: 

Sizing recommendation (conservative):
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100 (or equivalent) with contiguous capacity for the window Nov 18-20. This will give ~1.2k RPS headroom for chat-style workloads and handle KV cache pressure.
- Model: redwood-45b-q4 for primary (latency target ~220-300ms p95 under load); fallback redwood-13b-q4 to absorb overflow if QPS spikes beyond entitlement.
- KV cache: per-GPU KV cache footprint is limited; to avoid misses we should encourage Orbitly to provide warmup traffic targeting their most common prefixes. We do not offer a "cache pre-seed" API today; warmup is traffic-driven.

Warmup/canary plan:
1) Canary (Nov 16): 10% of expected peak for 60 minutes using synthetic traffic mimicking token lengths and top prefixes. Engineering will monitor KV hit-rate and p95 latency.
2) Ramp (Nov 18-19): 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 6-hour windows with rollback criteria (p95 > 400ms or error rate > 1%).

Operational notes / asks from Orbitly:
- Provide tokenization sample for a representative 500 requests so we can validate token counts and embedding sizes.
- Clarify geo split (NA/EU/APAC) — routing may land traffic on different pools; if APAC heavy we should plan a second smaller pool regionally.

I've attached a short perf estimate (redwood_perf_estimate.pdf) with expected p50/p95 numbers under the recommended configuration. If Orbitly can confirm traffic shape (chat vs batch) and the token samples, we can finalize the pool size and SLO exceptions.

-David

David Kim
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_perf_estimate.pdf)

Adding ops/CS runbook items — these have to be coordinated before we flip traffic: 

Pre-launch (by Nov 12):
- Schedule 60-minute canary with Orbitly engineers + Redwood on-call.
- Provide them a simple warmup script and prefer traffic that exercises top-10 prefixes.
- Ensure Orbitly's retry/backoff uses exponential with jitter and respects 429 headers.

During ramp:
- Enable detailed per-request tracing for the pool and capture token-level cost breakdown (we need these logs turned on ahead of the window).
- Prepare an on-call escalation matrix (CS lead, Eng on-call, infra).

Post-launch:
- 72-hour monitoring window with daily syncs for any quality/regression signals.

I also attached a runbook checklist that we can use as the basis for the call. We can convert to a shared doc once Diego compiles the MAP.

Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
(attachment: orbitly_runbook_checklist.md)

Sara — thanks for the details and the traffic matrix. We9ve reviewed internally and can support a temporary uplift with the following mutual action plan (MAP). Please review and confirm the items you can sign off on so we can lock capacity.

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Temporary entitlement: dedicated pool of 4x A100 peaking Nov 18-20. Expected headroom ~1.2k RPS; primary model redwood-45b-q4 with fallback redwood-13b-q4.
- Canary: Nov 16 14:00 PST — 60 minutes at ~10% peak. Redwood engineering and Orbitly on-call to observe KV hit-rate and p95.
- Ramp schedule: Nov 18 00:00 PST start -> 30% at 02:00 -> 60% at 08:00 -> 100% by 14:00. Rollback triggers: p95 > 400ms or error rate > 1%.
- Data we need from Orbitly by EOD Nov 6: tokenization sample (500 requests), final geo split, confirmation of chat vs batch % by endpoint, and signed DocuSign to provision the entitlement (link below).
- Runbook call: proposed Nov 10 at 10:00 PST to walk the checklist and assign owners.

Commercial note (Marissa/Karthik to follow up): we will provision the temporary pool as a time-limited entitlement. Marissa/Karthik — suggested commercial terms: one-week uplift flat fee + short-term discount if they convert to a monthly reserved pool.

Sara / Tim — please confirm the items above and upload the token sample. Once you confirm we will queue procurement and engineering to pin the pool. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/OPP-2026-0091
DocuSign sign-off: https://www.docusign.com/sign/Orbitly-Entitlement-Bump

Thanks — will send a calendar invite for Nov 10 runbook call after we get confirmation.

Diego Fernandez
